sample_unit: macular OCT B-scans (one per patient), read by 2 optometrists

links.outcome: Optometrist sensitivity for OCT abnormalities with vs without AI assistance versus expert reference
links.effect: Sensitivity rose from 61.6% to 98.6% (Optometrist A, p<2.0x10-8) and from 87.7% to 95.9% (Optometrist B, p=0.031); accuracy 79.0% to 86.5% and 91.5% to 92.5%, with modest specificity reductions.
links.quote: Sensitivity improved from 61.6% (95% CI 49.5-72.8) to 98.6% (95% CI 92.6-100.0) for Optometrist A (p<2.0x10-8) and from 87.7% (95% CI 77.9-94.2) to 95.9% (95% CI 88.5-99.1) for Optometrist B (p=0.031).

screen.reason: The study is a retrospective reader study evaluating the diagnostic performance of optometrists reading macular OCT scans with versus without AI decision support (CIRRUS PathFinder).
